Contents

On this page

Entries are dated and chronological. Each one carries what it was for, what was done, what came out, and who was there. The photographs are the team's own, filed by date.

What this page is, as of 25 September 2026

The months below are not bench entries yet. They are a dated index, assembled from facts already published on Plants, Parts, Measurement, Experiments, Engineering and Results, so that whoever writes the notebook has the skeleton of dates in front of them. Nothing here was taken from a source outside this wiki, and no date, number or name has been added that another page does not already carry. What is missing from every month is what a notebook is actually for: who was on shift, what was done step by step, and what the photographs of that day show.

March 2026

27 March. The plant work starts in somebody else's laboratory. The team visited Prof. Cheng Mei-Chun at NTU with no plants and no protocol, was walked through Arabidopsis on plates and through her group's hydroponic boxes, and came away with seed. The whole of Plants grows from that afternoon, and the hydroponic design on this project is a copy of hers.

April 2026

4 April. Dr. Verslues, Academia Sinica. A growth chamber full of vertical plates, which is where the vertical rack and its angle come from (Plants).

26 April. Three float plates cut by hand for three reservoir sizes, before anyone knew which hydroponic box would survive (Plants).

May 2026

10 to 27 May. Experiment set 1: NaCl at 50 and 100 mM against 1 mM trehalose, on round plates, scored as whole-seedling length. The finding is a protectant with a toxic ceiling, 14.6 mm for trehalose alone against a 51.7 mm control (Plants).

16 May. The 花博農民市集 farmers' market. Stallholders were asked what actually goes wrong in their fields, and salt was not the first answer (Plants).

19 to 26 May. The B. subtilis electroporation sweep. Yield rises from 2.0 to 2.3 kV and collapses by 2.5 kV; the first two pulses arced until 300 Ω was put in parallel. How many independent runs sit behind that window is disputed between the deck and Engineering, and the notebook is the record that would settle it (Measurement, M8).

20 May to 4 June. Experiment set 2, trehalose at 0.5 mM, which rescued nothing.

27 May to 12 June. Experiment set 3, two simultaneous trials that pointed opposite ways.

30 and 31 May. Float plates made by hand, and the first photography rig: a phone in a light box over a round plate (Plants).

June 2026

1 June. The photo stand the dry lab built, in use. Two photographs of one plate become comparable from here on.

3 June. Csn:Lea transformed, worked up on Engineering.

6 June. Version 1 of the reactor. It ended early on a leak at the pump head, which carries lumen-side culture, and 2 mL of shell-side liquid spread on LB grew nothing. That single plate is still the entire containment record of this project (Results, R8).

7 June. Seeds onto plates and into the cold, with an instructor at each elbow. Hydroponic prototype 4 took four-day-old seedlings across from agar instead of being sown with seed, and it is the one box of five that came through clean.

13 to 17 June. Boxes A and B on the rack; the first vertical plates into the chamber on 16 June; and on the 17th a rack loaded the wrong way round for a few days, which turned a root length experiment into nothing. Dr. Kyle's rule never to top up evaporated medium dates from the same week.

20 June. Prof. Chen Wen-liang on the reactor, the model and the planting device (Plants).

24 to 30 June. Cloning and plants at the same time: assembly B colony PCR on the 24th and assembly D on the 26th (Parts); experiment set 4 running from 17 June; and the 30 June root length row where two mould-covered seedlings were counted as part of the denominator but not the numerator (Measurement).

25 June. A session at DingXi Elementary. The date and the spelling of the school disagree with Education; see the review note below.

July 2026

1 to 3 July. Assembly D sequenced on the 1st, assembly B on the 3rd. Experiment set 4 read for chlorophyll on 2 July, which is the set where normalising to fresh weight inverts the ranking (Measurement).

9 July. CH Biotech. The team came back with 富肽2號, which became experiment set 7 at 1:500.

12 July. Experiment 5 trial 1, the day that appears twice in the root length workbook with different numbers in each block (Measurement, M7).

19 July to 3 August. Experiment set 6, the clean salt ladder, nine seedlings per group.

21 July. Two things at once: a day on Teacher Chen Hui-wen's farm, and the start of the long photometer run whose OD channel stops being a measurement at 243 h (Measurement).

22 to 28 July. Assembly C colony PCR on the 22nd and sequenced on the 24th; assemblies I and J sequenced on the 28th. Experiment set 7 begins on the 27th, and the vertical-plate photographs used as Figures 4 and 5 on Measurement are from that day. Hydroponic set 1 took its peptide on the 25th and its salt on the 28th.

30 and 31 July. Assembly A colony PCR at 1,833 bp and sequenced the next day. All twelve screened colonies of assembly L were called failed on the 30th, a call later contradicted by two gels (Parts, P14).

August 2026

2, 7 and 24 August. Three Western blots. Only the 24 August membrane has a ladder that resolves, and it carries one band at roughly 41 kDa in the 18 August lane, with the 23 August culture, the material already sprayed on plants, blank.

3 to 5 August. Set 6 scored at day 6 on the 3rd; hydroponic set 1 harvested on the 4th; and on the 5th the team found that absorbance had been read at 633 nm where the chlorophyll equation wants 663. That error still quarantines nine worksheets (Measurement, M4).

8 to 16 August. The long photometer run ends on the 8th. The pump flow and pressure runs are on the 13th and 14th, with no configuration written on either sheet, and the sweep that works, because it carries a jumper control, is on the 16th (Measurement, M12).

11 August. 源鮮智慧農場, a commercial hydroponic farm, and the same afternoon the dry lab was back on the hardware drawings.

15 to 21 August. The heat set, five days at 37 °C, in which no treated arm beat the control.

18 to 23 August. The set 8 pretest is sown on the 18th and abandoned when every ACCD plate grows bacteria; trial 1 is sown on the 21st and goes the same way after the 0.22 µm filtration is done on the open bench. The TiO2 linearity session is on the 23rd. Level 0 clones for the mutant cargoes are sequenced on the 19th and 20th (Parts).

26 to 29 August. The team minute of the 26th records the blot result in plain words. Assemblies P and R are sequenced the same day. On the 28th the team went back to Prof. Cheng with a progress report, 154 days after the first visit, and said which of her suggestions had not been done.

September 2026

1 to 6 September. Four modules in one plasmid: the Level 2 ACDI junctions are checked on the 1st, and the construct is junction-checked and not sequenced end to end (Parts). Prof. Cheng's rulings are written up on the 2nd. The 102-hour perfusion run, the clean growth record, runs from the 2nd to the 6th.

3 to 5 September. Assemblies Q and S sequenced on the 3rd, which makes them the most recent confirmed constructs. The green forum is on the 5th, and experiment 7 trial 4, the one internally coherent chlorophyll dataset in the archive, is read the same day.

9 to 19 September. Colony PCR on the BoPep4 units on the 9th; the ABDI device re-screened on the 17th; the Level 0 point mutants screened at 548 bp on the 18th, which is the first wet lab record of the dry lab's peptide designs existing as DNA; the three Level 2 junctions on three clones on the 19th.

22 and 23 September. The per-seedling root length workbook arrives in the data drop, which is what put a spread on the salt ladder, and Experiments, Parts, Plants and Measurement are written.
